title: Backcasting from Secure Multi-Agent Orchestration: What Architectural Constraints Are Necessary?

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from Secure Multi-Agent Orchestration: What Architectural Constraints Are Necessary?

**Problem:** Success state: a multi-agent orchestration system where no agent can take actions outside its authorized scope, even if compromised. Working backward, what architectural constraints are required?

**Direction:** Define the security properties of ideal multi-agent orchestration. Work backward to identify necessary architectural constraints (explicit permission manifests, inter-agent message signing, action sandboxing). Prototype the constraints in a simple multi-agent system and measure utility impact.

**Why it matters:** Multi-agent orchestration security is currently ad hoc. This study provides a principled architectural specification derived from first principles.

**Relevant context:** Multi-agent security; LW threat matrix; Anthropic multi-agent safety design.
